rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday choice when praising someone to make them feel good or win their favour.

example.english: I tried to flatter him so he would agree to help me.
example.traditional: 我氹佢幾句，想佢肯幫我。
example.jyutping: ngo5 tam3 keoi5 gei2 geoi3 soeng2 keoi5 hang2 bong1 ngo5

rows.note: Choose this when the praise is clearly flattering, insincere, or obsequious rather than ordinary praise.

example.english: They often flatter the boss because they want a promotion.
example.traditional: 佢成日奉承老闆，想升職。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 fung6 sing4 lou5 baan2 soeng2 sing1 zik1

rows.traditional: 將 A + V + 得好睇
rows.jyutping: zoeng1 A V dak1 hou2 tai2
rows.note: Use this for a portrait, photograph, film, or other depiction that presents A attractively.

example.english: This portrait is designed to flatter him, and even he likes it.
example.traditional: 呢幅畫將佢畫得好睇，連佢自己都鍾意。
example.jyutping: ne1 fuk1 waak6 zoeng1 keoi5 waak6 dak1 hou2 tai2 lin4 keoi5 zi6 gei2 dou1 zung1 ji3
